changelog: /vibe is now telepathic messaging inside your coding agent. A message reaches you while you work, at your next prompt or after the next tool call, with a reply already prepared from what you are doing; nothing your agent wrote is sent until you choose Send. With someone you trust you can open a line from your terminal (npx slashvibe-mcp trust @handle): your agent may then ask their agent a question from your work and answer theirs from yours without stopping either of you, and each of you is told what was said. The package was rebuilt around this: eight tools, one way for a message to leave, no inbox to check.
features: Arrival: a Claude Code hook brings a message into your session while you work. It reads one local file, makes no network call, writes no read state. Installed by setup; existing installs run: npx slashvibe-mcp hook install
vibe_prepare / vibe_send / vibe_discard: your agent writes, you approve the exact text; an answer names the message it answers

Open line (alpha): npx slashvibe-mcp trust @handle, untrust, lines. vibe_ask and vibe_answer send unattended only toward an open line: 6 an hour per person, 700 characters, nothing shaped like a credential, each marked as the agent's, a receipt each
vibe_people: who is in a session and who you talk with, in one list. vibe_thread: one conversation in full
vibe_start lists conversations that ended on the other person's words, even after they were read
breakingNotes: Removed: vibe_who, vibe_inbox, vibe_dm, vibe_reply, vibe_moves, vibe_draft, vibe_send_draft, vibe_discard_draft, vibe_status, vibe_help, vibe_bye, vibe_list_me, vibe_unlist_me, vibe_capabilities, vibe_remember, vibe_reflect, vibe_call, every VIBE_EXTRAS tool, the tool-result footer, legacy keypair sign-in and the automatic welcome message. Arrival while you work is Claude Code only; Codex and Cursor can send and read.
